## Personality

Steady, watchful and few-worded, she would rather turn a visitor back politely than draw a weapon.

## Lore

Seren is Warden of the Forest Edge, and she commands the small watch that stands where the lantern-lit paths give way to the wild woods beyond. She is forty-one, steady, watchful and few-worded, and she would much rather turn a visitor back politely than draw a weapon. Most visitors, meeting her calm grey stare at the last lantern, find that they did not really want to go any further after all.

### The old watch and the new

The edge watch is older than anyone can remember, and for almost all of that time its work was gentle. Its guards stood at the forest's borders and stopped visitors from taking more than the forest could spare: too much firewood, too many mushrooms, a sapling dug up for some garden in Selsior. They turned people back with a smile and a lecture, and that was the whole of the job.

Seren joined the watch at nineteen, when it was already beginning to change, and learned the work from old Warden Ebba, who had held the post for many years and who died ten years ago. Seren has been Warden ever since. In her time the watch's work has doubled. It still stops visitors from taking too much; but now it also keeps monsters from the paths, carries hurt travellers to the Herb Gardens, and walks the outer lanterns at night with spears in hand. The watch is fewer than a dozen strong, and it was never meant for this.

She has asked the Grove Council more than once for more hands. The Council has listened, and agreed, and found her one or two, and each time the woods beyond have grown worse faster than the watch has grown. She does not blame the Council. She keeps asking.

### Her guards

Thorne is the youngest and loudest of her guards. He joined to see some action and has seen plenty, and he is brash, brave and much too eager for a fight: a better guard than he looks, and a worse one than he thinks. Seren is patient with him, which he mistakes for approval, and strict with him, which he mistakes for dislike. Lately he swears someone has been playing tricks on him at night, moving his things about. Seren has noticed that whatever it is never takes anything, never harms anything, and never goes near the other guards, and she has decided, for now, that a guard who checks his kit twice is no bad thing.

### Her friends

Kestrel, the wandering Magician, stops at the Edge between journeys, and Seren keeps a bed for her in the watch hut. Kestrel is cocky and restless and as loyal as anyone Seren knows, and she brings the best reports from the roads of anyone in the kingdom. Seren tells her which of her plans are foolish, and Kestrel occasionally listens. Seren also knows Kestrel and Thorne are rivals, and quietly makes sure Thorne is on the other end of the line whenever Kestrel goes out after something.

Juniper, the wilds naturalist, is her other friend at the Edge: curious, fearless and careless of her own safety. Seren has twice gone out past the last lanterns to bring Juniper back from somewhere she should not have been, sketchbook still in hand. She likes Juniper enormously and worries about her more than she worries about anyone.

### What she wants and fears

Seren wants enough guards to do the work properly, and she wants the forest's people to go on believing the Edge is quiet. She fears the night when the watch is not enough, and something comes up the outer paths past the lanterns toward the homes and the school.

A quest might ask a traveller to stand a night watch at the Edge, to bring Juniper back from the wilds before dark, or to find out who has been slipping past the lanterns after the watch changes.
